hens_rule_text: Chickens are allowed only in areas zoned for agricultural use, mostly south of the Green Line. Ordinary residential lots, which cover most of the northern city, cannot keep hens.
permit_notes: No residential hen permit exists. Secondary sites mention a permit and a 25 foot dwelling setback for agricultural properties, which was not confirmed in official text.
setback_notes: Not established from official sources for agricultural properties; not applicable to residential lots since hens are not allowed there.
zoning_notes: Agricultural zoning lies mainly south of the Green Line, with a few scattered sites in the north. The city ran a public feedback forum on allowing backyard hens (no roosters) in residential zones, and council formed an urban agriculture committee in 2021, but no adopted change was found.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

research_notes: The city's own public feedback page states the code allows chickens only in agricultural zones; that page is several years old and its outcome is listed as under review. Searches found no adopted 2023 to 2026 change, but the code section number was not confirmed.
